summary: CI runners evicted from long-running builds after gateway JWT signing-key rotation
description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled rotation of the API gateway's JWT signing key, in-flight CI/CD builds that had been running for >30m experienced authentication rejections and were force-evicted. Impact: Multiple long-running release and e2e pipelines across internal clusters failed mid-run with HTTP 401/403 on subsequent agent heartbeats and artifact uploads. Environment: internal CI fleet (self-hosted runners) in k8s clusters: ci-us-east-1-a, ci-eu-west-1-b. Rotation window: 2026-03-10 03:00-03:15 UTC.

Observed symptoms: runner websocket connections stayed open but CI jobs reported 'authorization failed' when trying to POST logs or renew session tokens; some runners retried and re-registered successfully, others aborted and left orphaned pods. No node restarts. No Vault rewrap coincident with event (Vault Ops confirms no rewrap during that window).

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Start a long-running job (>20m) on a self-hosted runner that periodically renews its session via /agent/refresh (JWT header).
2) Rotate gateway JWT signing key and replace JWKS endpoint served by the gateway without a dual-key grace period.
3) Observe the runner's next refresh attempt being rejected with 401 and build aborting.

Logs / errors (representative):
- runner-agent[pid]: POST /agent/refresh -> 401 Unauthorized {"error": "invalid signature"}
- ci-orchestrator: job 12345 -> Cancelled: authentication failure during artifact upload
- gateway-audit: key_id change event: old kid=gw-sig-v12 -> new kid=gw-sig-v13 (2026-03-10T03:05Z)

Workaround applied: Re-deployed gateway with dual-JWKS support (accept both old and new kid) and restarted CI ingress to allow older tokens for 10m grace period. Affected long-running jobs were retried from last checkpoint where possible.

Request: Post-rotation runbook and safer rotation procedure for gateways that sign agent-facing tokens; consider deploying a) key rollover support with overlap, b) token versioning/rotation TTL recommendations for runner SDK, and c) detection/alerting for mass 401 spikes tied to key rotations.
comments: 2026-03-10 - 03:22 UTC - Maya Patel: Triage started. Reproducer attempts queued against ci-us-east-1-a. Noticed 401s spike at 03:05 UTC correlating with gateway key_id change.

2026-03-10 - 04:10 UTC - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Confirmed gateway published new JWKS and removed old key immediately. Rolling back to accept both keys reduced failures. Patching gateway to support key overlap now.

2026-03-11 - 09:14 UTC - Release Eng (Priya Nair): Affected two release pipelines (release/2026-03-09-candidate and nightly-e2e). We saw mid-run cancellations; will rerun jobs that support checkpointing. Requesting a formal runbook to avoid recurrence.

2026-03-12 - 11:05 UTC - Auth Eng (Noah Kim): Draft PR added to infra repo to add dual-key acceptance and JWKS versioning. Also adding metrics to alert on >5% agent 401 rate within 5m after any key rotation event. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4890
investigation_notes: Correlation matrix shows 401 spike exactly aligned with gateway key_id rotation event timestamp (03:05 UTC).

Runner SDK uses JWTs signed by gateway and refreshes every 60s; tokens have 10m TTL. During rotation we lacked a grace window in gateway, so tokens signed with old key were rejected immediately at first refresh after 03:05.
No Vault KMS rewraps or service account key changes detected in the same window; authentication failure localized to gateway signature verification.

Some runners retried with a fresh registration flow and obtained new tokens successfully; long-running jobs that did not trigger a full re-registration remained stuck because their vended token was still valid but rejected by signature check at refresh step.
Hypothesis: immediate key replacement without JWKS overlap caused stateless auth to break for any actor that held tokens signed by old key but attempted operations validated against the new JWKS.
We also observed an edge-case where proxies with aggressive caching of JWKS (internal CDN) continued serving stale keys for ~2m, causing a mixed verification environment.
resolution_notes: Short-term: Reconfigured gateway to accept both old and new signing keys for a 15m overlap window during rotations. Deployed fix to CI ingress to clear JWKS CDN caches faster.
Medium-term: Merged PR implementing graceful key rollover and JWKS versioning (infra PR #4890). Added a deploy-time verification step that exercises agent refresh flow before finalizing key switch.

Long-term actions: Update runbook to require a minimum 10m overlap when rotating gateway signing keys, add monitoring alert that ties key rotation events to agent 401 rates, and update runner SDK to detect key-rotation-related 401 and automatically attempt re-registration flow with exponential backoff.
Follow-up: Schedule knowledge-transfer with Release Engineering to walk through runbook. Add a postmortem entry in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood-inference/internal/pm/postmortems/INT-99555
